Our pre-x138 files were never weighed as partners after probe 34: exp51 56527239 (exp48 + the x138 V1284 head, 0.950), exp52 56534391 (0.950) and exp48 56510845 (0.948). All are COMPLETE and could be ticked at no compute cost. WHAT CHANGED: in 744273 (11:53Z), Cyrus writes that 'the bigger changes may happen around solutions based on the public code anchor, especially those that do not rely on proper cross-validation and appear to be heavily overfitted to the public leaderboard'. You WeiLin (12:24Z) says his local best scores poorly on the LB. Our V_pub stacks two layers of public-LB tuning on the x138 anchor: x138's own tail and our cap 6 + K + CI. A partner that also drops the x138 tail would hedge one layer more than #37 does. RECOMPUTED with the R33-RC-A normal model (D = partner - V_pub on private, mu = -g*rho, E[D+]): #37 (g 0.005, s 0.0025) gives 0.49 / 0.21 / 0.09e-3 at rho 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.7. exp51 (g 0.009) at s 0.004 gives 0.72 / 0.26 / 0.10e-3, and at s 0.006 gives 1.44 / 0.79 / 0.45e-3. exp51 wins only if its private spread is at least 1.6x that of #37 and rho is low (<= 0.25), which is the 'heavy shake-up' world. NEW VERDICT: UPHELD (not revived). (1) exp51 is a public-anchor file too: the pilkwang weights, the sjlee101 stack whose knobs (DC 0.20, tight55) were chosen from sjlee's public forks, and the x138 head. The comment does not favour it over #37. (2) No off-public comparison of the x138 tail against the sjlee tail exists; the exp60 lab replays x138 only (F-TRN-15). So the larger spread s is a guess, and so is the sign of the tail swap. (3) The E[D+] gap is +0.00 to +0.23e-3 at matched assumptions, inside the model noise (R33: the whole partner decision is worth about 0.0002). (4) The user ticked P3 {exp87a 56640366, #37 56563521} at 12:37Z. Changing the partner on a comment with no numbers would be post-hoc, the pattern the JT-neighbour rejection (R34-RC-C) warns against.
